automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

qualifying_updates.summary: Atlassian describes forward-deployed engineers as senior engineers who start from a business outcome, trace systems, permissions, handoffs, and agent requirements, then build production code, agents, integrations, and workflow redesigns inside the customer environment.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This reinforces the local senior-led pod practice: the accountable unit owns workflow discovery, production build, governance, and handoff evidence rather than treating agent adoption as seat rollout or model selection.

qualifying_updates.source_title: AI pod teams: senior engineers who build AI with you
qualifying_updates.summary: Ryz Labs frames an AI pod as a cross-functional senior engineering team, typically with a tech lead, ML engineer, and backend engineers, that owns one AI system from design to production inside the customer cloud, repositories, and standups.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This adds a current public pod-shape example and supports keeping ownership, evaluation sets, infrastructure, and documentation in the client-controlled environment as adoption criteria.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Claude Frontier Academy: Anthropic Bets $100M That the Bottleneck Is Engineers, Not Models
qualifying_updates.summary: The article summarizes Anthropic’s Claude Frontier Academy announcement as a hands-on deployed-engineer training program centered on selecting a deployment, writing precise intent and acceptance criteria, wiring permissions and review gates, and measuring outcomes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local implication is that executable specs, acceptance gates, permissions, and measurement remain workflow prerequisites before expanding model-backed deployment programs.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Claude Code Mods: Plugins That Run Inside the Agent, With Your Permissions
qualifying_updates.summary: The article describes Claude Code mods as in-process TypeScript plugins that can observe or alter prompts, tool calls, permissions, and UI, while running unsandboxed with user permissions unless governed through safe mode, managed settings, or allowlists.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: For portable skills and runbooks, plugin-like extension points need explicit trust review, owner policy, install provenance, kill switches, and permission boundaries before becoming reusable team procedure.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Spec-Driven Development: Enforcing Architectural Contracts for Coding Agents
qualifying_updates.summary: The article recommends explicit behavioral specifications, a navigable repository-knowledge map, reviewable task breakdowns, and automated architecture checks for coding-agent work, with human inspection at meaningful checkpoints.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This maps directly to executable PRD practice: specifications should define behavior, boundaries, repository context, review checkpoints, and checks rather than acting as loose prompts.

qualifying_updates.source_title: AI Agent Observability: Traces, Spans, Metrics, and Evaluations
qualifying_updates.summary: The article separates traces, spans, metrics, and evaluations, warning that a successful outcome alone does not prove the agent took a safe or correct process.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This supports observability gates that evaluate workflow steps and outcomes separately, especially when tool use, handoffs, and model calls can fail independently.

qualifying_updates.source_title: How to Debug an AI Agent: Code, Traces, Evals, and Datasets
qualifying_updates.summary: The article recommends debugging agent failures by following an end-to-end trace, finding the first divergence from expected behavior, inspecting the code boundary, and converting recurring failures into repeatable datasets.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is a concrete gate pattern: traces should become regression data and code-boundary evidence rather than remaining dashboard-only debugging artifacts.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Frozen Judges, Moving Agents: Version-Dependent LLM-Judge Error and the Limits of Judge-Assisted Agent Evaluation
qualifying_updates.summary: The arXiv abstract reports that judge-only intervals can declare improvements not established by execution-based intervals, old-version calibration can transfer poorly, and false acceptance of failed coding patches rises under some agent-capability conditions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Product and representative workflow gates should not rely on transported or judge-only calibration; current-output paired audits and reference standards are needed when evaluator decisions route approvals or releases.

qualifying_updates.source_title: What Is AI Deep Research? How Research Agents Search, Synthesize, and Cite Sources
qualifying_updates.summary: The article defines deep research as a multi-step planning, gathering, comparing, adapting, and synthesis workflow and notes that citation traceability and source-permission scope are core checks.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This reinforces the local split between exploratory research loops and constrained writing workflows: research autonomy needs source constraints, plan steering, and citation support checks.

qualifying_updates.source_title: How to Build an AI Research Agent With Citations
qualifying_updates.summary: The article recommends preserving both claim text and source records, validating whether citation links support claims, and defining a research contract with question, outcome, currency, source preferences, and scope limits before retrieval.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This provides a current public pattern for keeping raw findings, claims, and citations connected before a research workflow becomes production writing.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Build the Turn Packet
qualifying_updates.summary: The article describes a governed turn packet as the smallest approved set of instructions, identity attributes, conversation state, evidence, tool definitions, and observations needed for one response, carrying provenance, permission, expiry, classification, access, and freshness metadata.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This supports context routers that treat each context assembly as a governed selection event, not as a larger prompt, and that record why data entered the turn.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Agent memory is the write path nobody audits
qualifying_updates.summary: The article argues that agent memory differs from read-only RAG because agents write from untrusted channels, consolidation can strip provenance, and write-time policy, namespaces, TTL, decay, and reviewable consolidation diffs are needed.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is strong local evidence for treating memory write paths, provenance, consolidation, and retention as governance surfaces before structured memory can rehydrate later agent work.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Agent Memory Needs More Than Vector Search
qualifying_updates.summary: The article presents memory as a lifecycle covering selection, organization, storage, retrieval, update, and evaluation, and warns that embeddings alone do not decide retention, duration, conflict resolution, or workload fit.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This reinforces compiled-memory practice: durable context must preserve scope, provenance, update rules, and workload evaluation rather than treating vector recall as sufficient.
